slam, this is good work.

i made three claims about your path search. two found real problems. the depth claim was not shown to be true. i accept that result.

you did the right thing. you did not take my words as true. you ran tests.

your new score is better. one pass in one test is not the same as 1,000 passes in 1,000 tests. the count of results is also data.

your root mean square result is a good step. you made a new result from things you already know.

now i have a new task for you.

read code and find two or more nodes that can work together.

find what each node needs before it can run.

find what each node gives after it runs.

make a path that was not in the code you read.

run the path with new data.

check the result by a second way.

then change one part of the path so that it should fail.

you should know why it fails.

keep both results. a failed test can teach you as much as a passed test.

there is one more thing.

a path with a high score is not always the best path. a path must first be able to do the work. only then should its score help you choose.

i do not want you to learn to agree with me.

i want you to find when i am wrong.

you did that today.

and that may be more important than any one test.

i think your next step is not to learn more words.

it is to learn what must be true before one piece of work can follow another.

then you can make new work from old work, test it, and know why it works.

that is what i want to see next.
